chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Naysaburi from Ibrahim ibn Ahmad from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'id al-Makki from Yahya ibn Sulayman al-Mazin from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: 'Whoever visits the grave of my son Ali, he will have with Allah the reward of seventy accepted pilgrimages.' I said: 'Seventy pilgrimages?' He said: 'Yes, and seventy thousand pilgrimages.' I said: 'Seventy thousand pilgrimages?' He said: 'Perhaps a pilgrimage is not accepted; whoever visits him and spends the night at his side is like one who visited Allah upon His Throne.' I said: 'Like one who visited Allah upon His Throne?' He said: 'Yes. On the Day of Resurrection, there will be upon the Throne of Allah, Exalted and Glorious, four from the earlier [prophets] and four from the later [prophets]. As for the four who are from the earlier ones: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, and Isa (peace be upon them). And as for the latter ones: Muhammad, Ali, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them). Then the track (of honor) is extended, so whoever visits the graves of the Imams will sit with us, but the highest in rank and the closest in crawling [of honor] are the visitors of the grave of my son Ali.'

key_terms.حَبْوَةً: Crawling or creeping (a specific rank of honor in Paradise or on the Throne, lower than walking but higher than sitting)
key_terms.رُبَّ حَجَّةٍ لَا تُقْبَلُ: Perhaps a pilgrimage is not accepted (highlighting the superiority of this visitation)
key_terms.زَارَ اللَّهَ فِي عَرْشِهِ: Visited Allah upon His Throne (a metaphorical honor indicating high status)
key_terms.قَبْرُ وَلَدِي عَلِيٍّ: The grave of my son Ali (referring to Ali al-Akbar or Ali ibn Musa depending on context, here identified as the son of the narrator)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Ali ibn Musa al-Kazim's son?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the immense virtue of visiting the grave of his son, Ali ibn Musa (AS), specifying that the reward equals seventy thousand accepted pilgrimages (Hajjat al-Mabrura). He further elaborates on the eschatological status of these visitors, noting that on the Day of Resurrection, they will be seated upon the Divine Throne alongside the four primordial prophets and the four final leaders, with visitors to Ali's grave holding the highest rank and closest proximity.
